## Historical audit — S0219, visible chunk 1 of 2

**Source:** `/srv/lab-disks/disk2/users/xymo/Documents/Codex/2026-11-02/scene-rsi-rsi-1-3d-blender/outputs/scene_rsi_v2_1/results/r2/scene_rsi_v2_1/C1/development/commons_187101683/trajectory.jsonl`. Citations below refer to this file’s JSONL lines; all cited observations are complete lines, not split fragments.

| Evidence | Observed operation or result |
|---|---|
| Student `model_request`, line 1 | The task was single-image indoor reconstruction with separate meshes and matching camera, framing, placement and materials. The image itself is not visible in this audit; the student’s scene inventory is an interpretation, not independently verified fact. |
| Student `model_response`, line 3; `execute` step 1, line 4 | The first program constructed multiple objects: architecture, sofa components and rotated pillows, table, two cup-and-saucer arrangements, a potted plant and curtain. It specified stems and handles, but code-level placement does not prove visually correct connections. It used procedural material variation, a 64 mm camera, world illumination and two area lights. |
| `execution_result`, line 5; `select`, line 6 | Step 1 reported `ok: true`, saved a render and scene, and was selected. The render log reports 16 samples despite the program requesting 48. This establishes a successful execution, not visual or geometric correctness. |
| Student `model_request`, line 7; `codex_session`, line 8 | The student was sent the reference and first render for comparison, with one execution remaining. The session records no tool calls; the images are not available for independent inspection here. |
| Student `model_response`, line 9; `execute` step 2, line 10 | The student’s own feedback identified wrong table-edge direction and foreground placement, a left cup too far left, flowers too tall and upholstery too pale. The executed revision rotated the table 25°, moved the cup, compressed the plant, darkened upholstery, changed curtain and textures, and reduced lighting while retaining the camera. These are actual code changes, not proof that the diagnosis or correction was right. |

**Teacher input and exploration.** No teacher message, detection, diagnosis, proposed update or evidence of adoption appears in this visible portion. The comparison request was runner feedback, not a teacher diagnosis. The student independently produced and revised programs; the recorded sessions show no external tool exploration (lines 2 and 8). The second program’s “feedback correction” comment is the student’s assessment, not independent verification.

**Outcome and uncertainty.** Step 1 succeeded technically; step 2 was launched, but its result and any final selection are outside the visible chunk. Overall outcome is therefore **unknown**, not a demonstrated formal success, algorithm failure, empty patch or technical interruption. Whether the revised table, cup and plant remain correctly supported or connected, whether object poses and occlusions match, and whether camera, light, texture or rendering discrepancies improved remain unresolved. Neither the reference nor either render can be visually checked from the supplied text.

**Lessons.** Transferably, a successful render and named components do not validate visual fidelity; a comparison-driven local revision is distinguishable from a verified improvement. Task-specific hypotheses here concern table orientation, cup position, flower height and upholstery color; their accuracy and the effects of changing several variables together remain untested in the visible evidence.
